findings.text: Removal helper for hypervisor consoles detaches an instance from global lookup, drops its port reference and hangs up any bound terminal.
Wakeup helper flags the background thread and wakes it, while the poll helper exposes pending input or output work without sleeping.
TTY driver allocation macro binds the callers module to the allocator, and the operations setter records the callbacks table in the driver object.
TTY reference release is a no-op in this configuration, and the throttled query reports the throttled flag from terminal state.
Flip buffer insertion offers a fast path for ordinary characters with room available and delegates otherwise, with helpers computing character and flag storage positions.
Virtio endian adapters convert sixteen and thirty two bit quantities according to the negotiated device byte order.

Hypervisor console setup overprovisions adapter count for future hotplug, establishes driver identity and operations, starts its worker before registration, and publishes the driver only after a barrier. Failures unwind thread and driver references.

New virtio ports start disconnected with cleared statistics, empty console geometry, no name or buffered input, and queues bound by identifier. Character device and system device creation precede queue priming and list publication.

Remote serial ports assume host presence and single port devices promote the port to console use while multiport devices skip immediate promotion. Successful creation announces readiness while failures announce unready status.
Console geometry updates apply exclusively to console designated ports and leave other ports untouched.

Receive queue priming repeatedly allocates page sized buffers and enqueues them until the queue indicates saturation, returning how many were added and releasing the in-progress buffer when enqueue fails.
Asynchronous notification is emitted only when a process registered interest and the guest side remains connected.
Port teardown discards any pending receive data and reclaims completed transmit buffers, with final object release occurring through reference counting.

Control handling drops packets for unknown identifiers except creation requests, reaffirms readiness on duplicate creation, rejects identifiers beyond the configured maximum, and ignores repeated naming or console promotion.

Transmit draining forwards buffered output to the backend, preserves unwritten bytes for retry, arms deferred wakeup when progress stalls or completes, and discards output on hard errors indicating absent peer.

Polling skips input when no terminal is attached or flow control is asserted, hangs up on peer disconnect indication, defers retry when backend needs more room or flip storage is exhausted, and pushes accumulated input after releasing locks.

Receive interrupts collect newly arrived data, preserve it for console and remote serial use while discarding it for unconnected generic ports, notify async waiters, wake sleepers, and trigger background processing when console input is pending.
Control work recycles each processed buffer back to its queue, while transmit completion wakes waiters. Interrupts for unknown queues simply drain and release buffers.
Queue priming holds the supplied lock only across the enqueue attempt, leaving allocation and failure release outside the critical section.
Port publication serializes list insertion under the device ports lock after local locks and wait structures are initialized.

Unplug removes list membership under the device lock, adjusts connection state and waiter notification under the input lock, detaches console membership under the global console data lock, and nulls the device link under the output lock to block concurrent transmit.
Console removal clears global index tables under console ownership plus the instance lock, while deliberately leaving interrupt state for later hangup cleanup.
Control processing releases the control queue lock while dispatching each message and reacquires it solely to fetch or return buffers.
Hypervisor polling holds the instance lock for output draining and input decisions, temporarily releasing it for scheduling, disconnect hangup, and final input delivery.

Host presence changes reclaim transmit completions under the output lock and emit async signals under the input lock, matching teardown which discards receive state and reclaims transmit state under the respective locks.
Each named port exposes a device directory group containing exactly one attribute for its name.

Diagnostic readout summarizes identity and connectivity, queue saturation, transfer and discard counters, and console designation with its terminal number, rendering console status as yes or no wording.
Resize messages carry a control header followed by two sixteen bit dimensions in device byte order representing columns then rows on the wire.
Character storage begins at the buffer base plus offset, while flag storage begins one capacity length beyond that character position.

Observed port state combines identifiers and queue handles, device and character device handles, input and output locks with a wait queue, connection flags and statistics, plus console window geometry and terminal number with async interest and reference count.

Port objects progress from allocation and device creation through list publication and readiness announcement to operation, then via unplug to list detachment, data reclamation, device destruction and deferred freeing.

Host control events drive creation, removal, console promotion with early boot completion, geometry update with resize handling, presence update with waiter wakeup, and one-time naming with userspace notification.

Poll outcome signals write pending when output remains and read pending when input may be available, throttled, backlogged, or truncated by atomic limits, with timing reset on activity and extended stall when output makes no progress.

Host presence follows explicit host messages and defaults true for remote serial, guest presence clears permanently on unplug after notifying interested processes, and either transition wakes waiters.
Deferred control work acts as the control queue drain, bounding each fetched length to buffer capacity before dispatch.
Queue interrupts serve as completion entries for transmit and receive paths, each dropping its reference after handling.
Name attribute reads and diagnostic file reads expose port identity and runtime state to userspace.
Console initialization entry allocates the terminal driver, brings up its worker thread, registers with the terminal layer and publishes the global handle.
Creation failures unwind in reverse order and still inform the host of unready status so management software can observe the outcome.
Malformed or out-of-range host identifiers never create state; unknown targets are dropped with diagnostics and oversized creation is warned and ignored.
Allocation exhaustion aborts priming with an error, enqueue failures release the tentative buffer, while a full indication during creation is benign because buffers persist across unplug.
Driver allocation, thread creation and registration failures each unwind only resources acquired so far and propagate the underlying error.
Concurrent transmit and close are fenced by nulling the device link under the output lock, preventing enqueue to torn down queues or stale control emission.
Large atomic reads are broken with deferred continuation to bound latency, and flip exhaustion or backend retry requests reschedule rather than busy loop.
Completions arriving for vanished ports are safely discarded without wakeups or reference operations beyond buffer release.
Name storage exhaustion or attribute creation failure leaves the port functional without userspace naming support, reporting the condition through diagnostics.
Hypervisor console driver uses identity hvc for driver and device naming, system type, raw plus reset termios behavior, worker title khvcd, and major plus minor bases from dedicated constants.
Virtio port character devices encode virtual device index and port identifier in vport naming, with minor number equal to port identifier under the device major.
Name attribute output is newline terminated, optional until host supplies a name, and triggers a change event on creation. Diagnostic files are world readable.
Host signaling distinguishes addition, removal, readiness affirmation, console designation, geometry change, presence change and naming, with readiness using one for ready and zero for failure.
Console geometry is a pair of sixteen bit row and column values, initialized to zero and updated only from host resize messages for console ports.
Multibyte control fields use device negotiated endianness, selecting little endian conversion when the device indicates little endian and big endian otherwise.
